why: A gate that fails every landing with the same historical findings is not a signal: a worker cannot tell the defect it caused from the ones history already carried. verify-version-tags still computes and prints every finding in this file, with its reason, on every run and on both refs; a pin only stops that one finding from failing the exit code. A pin that names no finding any more fails the gate, so this file can describe history and can never hide a new defect.
note: The identity of a pin is kind + version + sha + (for wrong-commit) the tag's commit. A tag moved onto a different wrong commit, a different declaring commit, or a finding that disappears is therefore a new fact, not this pin. A real defect pinned here carries the tag write that repairs it; when that write lands, the finding goes and the pin must be deleted, or the gate reports it as a stale pin.
